macro.regime: Payrolls shock flips Fed to a near-certain October hold; broad Friday rally meets persistent CCC-credit and BOJ/MAS tightening cross-currents
macro.narrative: September Non-Farm Payrolls, released on schedule Friday 2 Oct (no government shutdown is in effect; the 2 Sep stopgap funds the government through 11 Dec 2026), printed a sharp miss at +29,000 versus ~84-90K consensus, with unemployment rising to 4.2%, wage growth cooling to +0.1% m/m (+3.0% y/y, the lowest since May 2021), and a net -60K two-month downward revision to July/August. Markets read the miss as 'bad news is good news' for Fed policy: odds of an October 27-28 hold surged to roughly 80-83% (hike odds fell to ~17-18% from ~33-34% a day earlier), the 10-year Treasury yield fell, and US equities rallied broadly into the weekend -- S&P500 +0.73% to 7,722.72, Nasdaq +1.19% to 27,190.86 (touching an intraday record high), Dow +0.49% to 51,176.96, Russell2000 +0.94% to 2,832.89, with VIX collapsing -6.59% to 15.31. Precious metals and oil paradoxically pulled back on the day (GLD -0.68%, SLV -0.51%, WTI -1.73%) despite the dovish repricing, a profit-taking pause after a sharp multi-week run rather than a thesis reversal, while gold/silver miners (GDX +1.20%, SILJ +0.44%) bucked bullion weakness. Overnight in Asia, Tokyo's core CPI print came in hot at 2.7% y/y (vs 2.4% forecast, 1.8% prior, core-core 3.0%), strengthening the case for further BOJ tightening at the Oct 29-30 meeting after the Sep 18 hike to 1.25%, while MAS is separately expected to tighten its S$NEER slope a third consecutive time at its Oct 14 meeting given Singapore core inflation at a 2-year high of 2.2%. Credit remains the one clear cautionary signal: CCC-and-below OAS crossed the formal 1,007bps distressed threshold on 30 Sep, its widest since the 2023 SVB collapse, even as broad HY stays comparatively tight and equities rally.
